description.narrative:
The Open Government Partnership (OGP) is a multi-stakeholder initiative established in 2011, aimed at securing commitments from governments to promote transparency, empower citizens, fight corruption and harness new technologies to strengthen governance. OGP currently comprises 75 national and 104 local governments and thousands of civil society organizations. To become a member of OGP, governments must meet OGPs eligibility criteria, endorse a high-level Open Government Declaration, deliver a National Action Plan (NAP) developed through public consultations, and commit to independent reporting on their progress through the Independent Review Mechanism (IRM).
OGP launched its 2023-28 strategy in 2023, after a year-long consultation process with a large community of government leaders, public servants, civil society, international partners, media and others. The result is a renewed vision for OGP as a more political, values-based partnership rooted in specific actions, innovations, and ideas for more open and democratic governments that meet citizens expectations. OGPs mission as part of the new strategy is to inspire, connect, and enable an ever-growing community of reformers and champions from government and civil society to take action together. OGP will achieve this by pursuing five mutually reinforcing goals: Strategic Goal 1: - Build a growing, committed, and interconnected community of open government reformers, activists, and champions - Build a stronger, more political global coalition for open government - Invest in leadership development for reformers - Expand strategic alliances and partnerships to reinforce open government principles
Strategic Goal 2: Make open government central to how all levels and branches of government function and deliver on their priorities - Provide a flexible action framework fit for diverse contexts and needs - Support mainstreaming of open government at all levels and branches of government work - Be more responsive to windows of political opportunity
Strategic Goal 3: Protect and expand civic space - Encourage civic space action and cultivate champions - Enforce and periodically review OGP policies on civic space
Strategic Goal 4: Accelerate collective progress on open government reforms - Raise the bar on transparency, accountability, participation, and inclusion - Launch a Partnership-wide challenge to promote collective action on ten priority areas (more information on the Open Gov Challenge below)
Strategic Goal 5: Become the home of inspirational open government innovations, evidence, and stories - Develop, curate and share high quality content - Create spaces for people to share their stories and connect

Insatsen avser ett stöd till organisationen Open Government Partnership om totalt 45 MSEK under en treårsperiod 2019-2021.
Open Government Partnership är ett multi-intressent-initiativ som startade 2011 med syfte att övertyga regeringar om insatser för att främja öppenhet, stärka medborgarinflytande bekämpa korruption och använda gemensamt utvecklade metoder för att stärka samhällsstyrningen. Open Government Partnership består för närvarande av 79 nationella och 20 lokala regeringar och ett tusental civilsamhällesorganisationer. För att bli medlem i Open Government Partnership måste regeringar uppfylla de villkor som är uppställda, göra ett offentligt uttalande om öppenhet, utverka en nationell handlingsplan med hjälp av medborgarkonsultationer och rapportera utvecklingen med hjälp av den oberoende översynsmekanism som finns i initiativet.
Open Government Partnerships vision är formulerad som att "fler regeringar ska bli mer transparenta, mer ansvarstagande och mer lyhörda för sina medborgares deltagande med slutgiltigt mål att förbättra styrning och samhällsservice". Arbetet kretsar kring nationella handlingsplaner som tas fram i en gemensam process mellan regeringar och civila samhället. Open Government Partnership arbetar utifrån en strategi som uppdaterades 2016 och utgör vägledning för verksamheten. Strategin kommer att utvecklas under 2019 för att med utgångspunkt i nuvarande vision formulera vägar för att nå bättre genomslag fram till 2022.
Strategin omfattar följande områden: 1) Ökat fokus på medborgarcentrerad samhällsstyrning 2) Breddat gemensamt ägarskap för nationella handlingsplaner 3) Ökad ambitionsnivå och lärande 4) Stärkt kapacitet, koordinering och nätverk för genomförande 5) Översyn av incitaments- och regelstruktur 6) Stärkt varumärke och kommunikationsstrategi
Total budget för 2019 är ca 12,4 MUSD. Budgetarna för 2020 och 2021 är uppskattade till 13,4 MUSD. Total budget är ca 39,2 MUSD. Sidas bidrag utgör knappt 10 %.

The intervention concerns support of 45 MSEK during the three-year period 2019-2021.
The Open Government Partnership (OGP) is a multi-stakeholder initiative established in 2011 aimed at securing commitments from governments to promote transparency, empower citizens, fight corruption and harness new technologies to strengthen governance. OGP currently comprises of 79 national and 20 local governments and some thousand civil society organisations. To become a member of OGP, governments must meet OGP's elibility criteria, endorse a high-level Open Government Declaration, deliver a National Action Plan (NAP) developed through public consultations, and commit to independent reporting on their progress through the Independent Review Mechanism (IRM).
OGP is directed by a strategy for 2015-2018 that was "refreshed" in 2016 to more clearly articulate the vision and identify the best means to work for that. By early 2020 OGP will complete a medium-term planning process, with the goal of developing a three-year implementation plan and budget (2020-2022). This implementation plan will not lay out a new vision for OGP but will focus on collective results that are aimed to be achieved in three years and how this will happen.
The strategy focusses on the following areas: 1) Deepen citizen-centered gocvernance 2) Broaden collective ownership of OGP domestically 3) Raise collective ambition, peer exchange and learning across OGP countries 4) Strengthen capacity, coordination and coalitions for implementation 5) Review performance incentives and rules of engagement 6) Strengthen the OGP brand and communications strategy
The total budget for 2019 is about 12.4 MUSD. The budgets for 2020 and 2021 are estimated to 13.4 MUSD respectively. Total budget amounts to approximately 39.2 MUSD. Sida's contribution constitutes a little less than 10 % for each year.

description.narrative:
Examples of achieved results presented by OGP in their Annual Report for Operational Year April 1st, 2024 -March 31st, 2025 connected to each of the Strategic Goals SO1-SO5:
SO 1. Build a growing, committed, and interconnected community of open government reformers, activists and champions
* REGIONAL MEETINGS: OGP and host governments cohosted three regional meetings during the year (in South America, Asia and Africa incl. the Middle East) providing valuable opportunities for reformers to connect, inspire each other, and build political support as they work to advance reforms. During the regional meeting in Brazil with 1200 participants, OGP together with OECD, and the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) co-organized a high-level anticorruption roundtable, bringing together key government, civil society, and donor representatives to align collective goals in fighting corruption. The session emphasized collective action between government, civil society, media, and the private sector, with participants highlighting OGPs role as an effective platform for implementing anticorruption commitments. The regional meetings demonstrate OGPs commitment to building a growing, interconnected community of reformers while advancing the key objectives of the 2023-2028 strategy. The meetings serve as critical platforms for sharing experiences, strengthening networks, and generating momentum for ambitious open government reforms. The regional meetings are also stepping stones for governments and civil society to refine the commitments in the Action Plans before the at the time upcoming OGP Global Summit in Vitoria-Gasteiz, Spain, in October 2025.
* CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT: OGP is partnering up with Apolitical to develop a comprehensive open government course for public servants, with support from the UKs Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office. This collaboration leverages Apoliticals platform, which reaches a quarter of a million public servants from 160 countries, to expand OGPs educational outreach. The course covers four to five sections including cross government reforms and deep dives into topics such as procurement and digital transformation, designed to help institutionalize open government practices within public administrations through scalable, practical learning resources. Course content is set to be finalized by June 2025, with an official launch before the end of the year.
SO 2. Make open government central to how all levels and branches of government function and deliver on their priorities
* NUMBER OF ACTION PLANS: In 2024, 95% of OGP countries (71 out of 75) implemented an OGP action plan. 10 new action plans were submitted in 2024, following a near record year in 2023 with 55 action plan submissions, and reflects OGPs new flexibility allowing for gaps between action plans.
* GROWTH: The Partnership continues to grow, with three new national members (Maldives, Zambia, and Benin) and 55 new local members joining during the year.
* ANTI-CORRUPTION: OGP strengthened global anticorruption efforts through strategic engagement in influential international forums. Notably, OGP contributed to the European Commission's guidance on anticorruption in key Global Gateway sectors, and shaped the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC) Implementation Review Mechanism initiative through strategic participation in six major forums.
* Country example Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republics efforts, with support from OGP, led to the country's new OGP National Action Plan (2024-2028) which includes three judiciary commitments the first time courts have formally participated in the countrys OGP work. This achievement has positioned the Dominican Republic as an emerging regional leader in open justice. One method for building momentum during the process was OGP organizing a learning exchange with Costa Ricas judiciary in order for Dominican officials to see open justice reforms in action. The Dominican Republics journey to integrate its judiciary into open government reforms exemplifies OGPs strategy to expand open government across all branches of government.
* Country example Moldova: The OGP's Support Unit (the Secretariat) strategically capitalized on the momentum generated by Moldovas EU accession process to firmly reestablish OGP on the national agenda. By framing open government reforms as essential components of EU integration requirements, the OGP SU helped Moldovan reformers align their efforts in its 5th action plan with commitments related to public participation relevant to EU accession, monitoring implementation of access to information laws, and ensuring transparency in anticorruption efforts.
* LOCAL LEVEL: A new OGP Local Co-Creation Playbook was published in three languages (English, Spanish and French), providing a comprehensive resource with guidance, examples, templates, and practical advice for effective cocreation processes tailored to local contexts. OGP prioritized this since evidence has shown that a good cocreation process contributes to better design and more impactful commitments in the Local Action Plans.
* LOCAL LEVEL: OGP expanded strategic partnerships for local impact, working with partners such as People Powered and Humanitarian Open Street Map Team to provide direct financial and technical support to 29 local members, enhancing their capacity to implement ambitious reforms.
SO 3. Protect and expand civic space
* CIVIC SPACE: 202425 saw a slight improvement in the number of civic space commitments across the Partnership as compared to previous years, with approximately one third of OGP countries now implementing civic space commitments. This growth has been primarily driven by increased commitments around freedom of association and expression, with several countries focusing specifically on funding mechanisms for civil society organizations. Despite this positive trend, the percentage of OGP countries passing the so called Open Government values check has declined over time, mirroring similar declines in non-OGP countries. More than 30 OGP members conducted elections in 2024 and political transitions were creating windows for civic space reforms in some contexts, while threatening regression in others. Early evidence suggests that the value of the OGP platform itself, improvements in the quality of dialogue as measured by Multi-Stakeholder Platforms (MSFs), and reasoned responses can help expand civic space, though this pattern requires further research.
*Country example Philippines: OGP as a technical platform. During its previous administration, civil society and government champions in the Philippines strategically framed OGP as a technical/innovation space to advance reforms like open contracting during periods where civic space has become more restricted in the country. This deliberately apolitical framing and approach helped to avoid drawing negative political attention while still maintaining progress on open governance in engagement with civil society. An independent evaluation of OGP by Oxford Policy Management in 2022 found that the OGP platform had become one of the few remaining safe spaces for civil society dialogue with government amidst closing civic space. N.B: Sida notes that this was reported in last year's Annual report as well, but finds it important and therefore highlights the result once again.
SO 4. Accelerate collective progress on open government reforms
* OPEN GOV CHALLENGE: Progress on the Open Gov Challenge: Commitments in Action Plans (both national and from local jurisdictions) connected to the so called specific Open Gov Challenge. As of March 2025, 73 commitments have been successfully submitted to the Challenge by 24 national members and 24 local jurisdictions (member and nonmember). Anticorruption is the most popular Challenge area with 20 commitments made thus far, followed by public participation with 14 commitments, and justice with nine commitments. The regional overview of Commitments in Action Plans showed that the Americas have made more Challenge commitments than any other region so far and that the region Africa and the Middle East is the first region to make at least one commitment across every of the 10 challenge area. The Open Government Challenge is a call to action from 2023 for all members of OGP to raise ambition in ten areas of open government to help strengthen democracies. The commitments should be achieved by March 2028, meaning the end of the current OGP Strategy. One example of an Open Gov Challenge from Ghana on Commitment on combating information and disinformation: In Ghana, digital platforms have been increasingly misused to spread misinformation and disinformation, threatening to undermine democracy. To address this, the government has made a commitment to collaborate with civil society and conduct a human rights assessment of existing legislation on misinformation and disinformation while protecting free speech, alongside fact checking, media literacy, and public education initiatives. OGP in 2024 also created The Open Gov Challenge Tracker, which was a new public repository to track eligible commitments to the Open Gov Challenge. The tracker serves as a transparent accountability mechanism for monitoring progress across member countries and local jurisdictions.
* Over the past year, 100% of OGP national members received support via the OGP Support Unit (SU) or via the OGP Independent Reporting Mechanism (IRM) in the form of peer exchanges, technical support, or brokered financial support. Among these, 65 countries participated in at least one peer exchange all 76 countries received technical support and 13 countries received brokered financial support. These support mechanisms were facilitated for various purposes such as supporting onboarding, action plan co-creation and implementation building CSO coalitions orienting members to the Open Gov Challenge political re-engagement and national- local collaboration, among others.
* GENDER AND INCLUSION: OGP continued to mainstream gender equality and inclusion as a key priority and crosscutting component of open government. Widespread interest from OGP members and dedicated support has helped to position gender and inclusion as the third most popular thematic area for OGP commitments, with nearly 60% of OGP countries with an active action plan currently implementing a gender-related commitment. In 2024, OGP advanced gender-focused reforms in intersectional ways across gender-responsive justice, gender-sensitive budgeting, online gender-based violence, and inclusive civic space. OGP also integrated gender perspectives throughout the Open Gov Guide, offering gendered examples and dimensions across thematic areas such as beneficial ownership, automated decision-making, open budgets, and access to justice, with dedicated chapters on gender-based violence and open gender data. This mainstreaming approach has successfully positioned gender and inclusion not only as a standalone priority, but as an essential lens for all open government reforms. '
SO 5. Become the home of inspirational open government innovations, evidence and stories.
* The OGP National Handbook was revamped in 2024 into a more user-friendly and streamlined resource and is available as a fully online version for the first time now. The new Handbook brings together everything OGP country stakeholders need to know about participating in OGP, with clearer rules and guidance for each part of the process. It also expands the Action Framework with distinct participation pathways and requirements for judicial branch institutions and national autonomous institutions etc.
* IMPACT LEVEL: Open Government Journeys is a new series online, documenting long-term reform stories from OGPs oldest members. See examples from Kenya, Philippines etc. on https://www.opengovpartnership.org/irm-guidance-overview/irm-open-government-journeys/
While an individual commitment in an OGP Action plan can show a snapshot of progress, it does not tell the whole story. In this series, the IRM explores the challenges, major achievements, and the future of open government in some of OGPs longest members to tell that story. Understanding the steps it takes to shift the status quo to more transparent, accountable, and responsive governance holds lessons for all reformers looking to apply open government principles to real world challenges.
Conclusion: Sida assesses the achieved results as overall satisfying for the operational year.
